ch15_lab_ai.title: Quick Check: AI, Machine Learning & Ethics

questions.q: What is the primary difference between Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML)?
options: They are exactly the same thing with two different names
AI is the broad concept of machines acting smartly; ML is a specific subset where machines learn and improve from data over time
ML is a type of hardware; AI is a type of software
AI only refers to robots, ML only refers to chatbots

questions.q: What is Algorithmic Bias primarily caused by?
options: A computer's processor overheating
Biased or incomplete training data, meaning the system inherits human prejudices found in the data it was given
Users typing prompts too quickly
A lack of internet bandwidth

questions.q: What is the 'Black Box Problem' in AI?
options: When an AI runs out of storage space
The inability to understand exactly how the AI reached a particular decision
When an AI is trained on too little data
A hardware malfunction in a server rack

ch15_lab_immersive.title: Quick Check: AR, VR & IoT Security

questions.q: What is the key difference between Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR)?
options: They are identical technologies with different marketing names
AR overlays digital content on top of the real world (you still see your surroundings); VR fully replaces the real world with a simulated environment
VR only works on phones; AR only works with headsets
AR is fully immersive; VR just adds overlays

questions.q: What makes Mixed Reality (MR) different from basic AR?
options: MR has no visual component at all
In MR, digital objects are anchored to and interact with the physical world -- e.g., a virtual ball can roll off a real table
MR only works with voice commands
MR is just a cheaper version of VR

questions.q: Why are IoT devices like smart refrigerators frequently targeted by hackers?
options: They contain more processing power than laptops
They often ship with weak default passwords and are rarely updated by users, making them an easy backdoor into a home or business network
They are too expensive to secure properly
IoT devices cannot connect to the internet at all

questions.q: What is a PWA (Progressive Web App)?
options: A website that only works on desktop computers
A web app that uses service workers and a manifest file to behave like a native mobile app -- installable on a home screen, works offline, and sends push notifications
A programming language for building APIs
A type of database used for e-commerce

questions.q: What does JAMstack stand for, and why are JAMstack sites so fast?
options: Java, Angular, MySQL -- because it uses a lightweight database
JavaScript, APIs, and Markup -- because it serves pre-built static HTML files via CDN, with no server rendering HTML on-demand
Just Another Modern stack -- it has no real technical meaning
JSON, AJAX, Markdown -- because it avoids using HTML entirely

questions.q: Conceptually, how does Web 3.0 primarily differ from Web 2.0?
options: Web 3.0 removed JavaScript entirely from the web
Web 3.0 focuses on decentralization (like blockchain) rather than centralized corporate servers
Web 3.0 is just a faster version of Web 2.0 with no other differences
Web 3.0 only works on mobile devices
